newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian bank Koper to buy 40 percent of M Banka.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian bank Koper to buy 40 percent of M Banka.

text.p: Slovenia's fourth largest bank, the unlisted Banka Koper, said on Thursday it would buy 40 percent of the shares of the smaller M Banka by the end of this year.
"We want to buy into M Banka in order to form a banking group where the two banks would cooperate in certain areas," Banka Koper's executive director Dusan Hocevar told Reuters.
The Bank of Slovenia has already agreed to the purchase.

The group would be the fourth banking group in the country following the July merger of bank SKB and UBK, the formation of a banking group of nine banks around state-owned Nova Ljubljanska Banka earlier this year and the establishment of a group of banks Celje and Hmezad in January.

Analysts said further mergers can be expected in Slovenia's overcrowded banking sector over the next couple of years as banks aim to reduce costs and prepare for the tougher foreign competition made possible by a new bank law that is expected to be adopted by parliament later this year.
The law would enable foreign banks to open branches in Slovenia. At present they can only set up subsidiaries requiring substantial capital outlays.
Currently there are 28 banks in Slovenia, although the country has a population of only two million. Four banks are in majority foreign ownership.
Bank Koper has a market stake of six percent while its balance sheet assets firmed to 99.7 billion tolars ($598 million) at the end of 1996 from 82.6 billion.

M bank has a market stake of 0.8 percent with balance sheet assets of 12.9 billion tolars at the end of last year, up from 12.2 billion. -- Marja Novak, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439 ($ = 166.7 Slovenian Tolars)
